content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text labels the Isaiah 7:14 link UNDERDETERMINED partly because the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways, which treats the verse as open to two meanings.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.","room":"When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open — I weighed whether the judge's word-count-cuts-both-ways phrase treats the verse as open to two meanings (breach) or merely notes cross-verse lexical evidence (clean).","why":"The judge marks the Isaiah 7:14 question UNDERDETERMINED because the word-count cuts both ways, but K-S2 says a verse with two meanings at once is not open and both meanings stand."}
